newsitem.title: UK: British drug czar must not wage police war-experts.
newsitem.headline: British drug czar must not wage police war-experts.

text.p: British experts on addiction warned the government on Friday that its planned new 'drug czar' must not wage a police war but should instead harness science to fight illegal drugs.
The new Labour government has advertised for a drug czar to fight growing illegal drug use in the country. The position mirrors one in the United States.

John Strang, director of the National Addiction centre in London, and colleagues welcomed the idea. "It is good news that the new Labour government is evidently serious about the growing national and international drug problem," they wrote in the British Medical Journal.

"But there is a grave danger that the increased political attention could backfire, producing a more politicised approach to the problem and causing the new czar's dominant orientation to be one of control."
Strang and his colleagues said it would be easy to make a show of fighting drugs.
"It could lead to a mistaken bias to funding more panda (police) cars, prisons, and pop propaganda instead of evidence-based treatment, rehabilitation, and preventive strategies," they wrote.
"Prisons are already bursting with new inmates," they added.
